races.paceDynamic: Salvator Mundi and Mighty Bandit will engage early as confirmed front-runners, with Salvator Mundi's natural speed likely edging the lead through the early stages. The prominent trio of Be Aware, Kala Conti and Alnilam will track close behind, while No Questions Asked sits deeper as the sole hold-up horse. Both leaders have the class to sustain a strong gallop over this 2m trip on testing ground, creating an honest pace that will stretch the field. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track the early pace and strike late, as they'll have the tactical advantage over both the vulnerable leaders and the isolated hold-up horse.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the two leaders clash early and weaken each other in the closing stages
scenarios.body: The honest pace sets up perfectly for Be Aware, Kala Conti or Alnilam to sweep past the tiring front-runners. Their prominent positioning allows them to stay in touch without doing the donkey work, then capitalize when the leaders pay for their early efforts.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Salvator Mundi or Mighty Bandit can repel their rival and maintain stamina reserves
scenarios.body: The survivor benefits from eliminating their main pace rival early, then controls the race from the front with softer fractions. Salvator Mundi's superior class gives him the edge if both are still traveling well turning for home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes truly searching and multiple horses tie up in front
scenarios.body: No Questions Asked gets the perfect setup from his patient position, with tired horses ahead providing stepping stones. Ben Jones can weave through weakening rivals as the only fresh finisher, though he needs significant pace collapse to succeed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders go too hard early and the prominent horses also get drawn into speed
scenarios.body: The race becomes tactical in the final half-mile with multiple horses coming back to the field. This creates a sprint finish that could suit any horse with a turn of foot, making form figures less reliable than tactical positioning.

watchPoints.text: Salvator Mundi and Mighty Bandit immediately clash for the lead and compromise each other's winning chances through excessive early pace
No Questions Asked gets shuffled back too far if the pace isn't strong enough, leaving Ben Jones with impossible task from rear
Kala Conti's jumping under pressure after 70-day break, as any mistakes will be costly in a race likely decided by small margins
Be Aware's response to headgear removal, as Harry Skelton may need to be more aggressive without the visual aids

races.paceDynamic: Push The Button, Fortune Timmy and Hold The Serve will ensure a fierce gallop from the start, with Push The Button's long absence making him vulnerable to crack early. The strong pace will stretch this 22-runner field and test stamina severely over 3m½f on testing ground. Nine horses wanting prominent positions creates a traffic nightmare approaching the business end. This setup heavily favours patient hold-up horses who can stay out of trouble and deliver late kicks when the pace collapses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the three confirmed leaders maintain a strong gallop and the prominent pack gets congested 2-3 out
scenarios.body: The fierce early pace will collapse the field and allow patient hold-up horses to sweep past tired leaders. Those held back can avoid the mid-race scramble and find cleaner passages late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent horses can secure an ideal position just behind the leaders without getting caught in traffic
scenarios.body: A horse like Absolutely Doyen or Supremely West travels kindly in the slipstream before striking when the pace drops. Their tactical speed gives them the edge over pure hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If Push The Button's long layoff tells and the other two leaders fail to maintain the gallop
scenarios.body: The race becomes a tactical affair where prominent horses can dictate and kick clear before hold-up horses get organized. Mid-division runners with tactical speed benefit most from the moderate tempo.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Hold The Serve or Fortune Timmy find the testing ground to their liking and maintain a sustainable rhythm
scenarios.body: Their recent good form and proven stamina allows them to repel all challengers in a truly-run staying test. The slower ground plays into the hands of those who can grind out the finish.

races.paceDynamic: Montemares, Masked Man, and Came From Nowhere will ensure a strong gallop from the start, with all three natural front-runners likely to contest the early lead. This sustained pace will test stamina reserves over the extended 2m4f trip on testing soft ground at Aintree. The relentless gallop will set up a searching examination of stamina in the closing stages. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can conserve energy early and produce late finishing kicks when the pace takes its toll.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners maintain a genuine gallop throughout and compromise each other
scenarios.body: The strong early pace will drain the leaders' stamina reserves, allowing closers like Bossman Jack, Soldier Reeves, and Scorpio Rising to pick up the pieces in the final furlong. Their patient tactics and proven stamina will prove decisive when the pace collapses.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Ballyfad or Rooster Crowing can sit just behind the pace-setters without getting involved in early skirmishes
scenarios.body: These horses can track the strong pace without expending excessive energy, then strike when the leaders weaken approaching the final flight. Their tactical position allows them to respond to moves while having enough in reserve for the finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three leaders can establish a clear advantage and dictate their own fractions
scenarios.body: Came From Nowhere has the best recent form and experience to potentially steal a march on his two pace rivals and maintain just enough in the tank. His superior fitness edge from a recent run could prove crucial in a stamina test.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Package
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and allows an unconsidered horse to benefit from the chaos
scenarios.body: The strong pace could set up perfectly for a horse like Zanndabad returning from a break or Lord Byron improving significantly from his last run. Fresh legs and a patient ride could exploit the tactical carnage.

races.paceDynamic: Lookaway leads as the sole confirmed front runner after Myretown's withdrawal, with support from prominent runners Bad, Imperial Saint, Leave Of Absence and Konfusion tracking close behind. The soft ground over 3m1f will ensure a searching test that gradually exposes stamina limitations. Without a second genuine pacesetter to press Lookaway early, the gallop may become steadier than ideal through the middle sections before intensifying from three out. This tactical setup strongly favours hold-up horses like Deep Cave, Mr Hope Street and Chance Another One who can exploit the likely kick finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace Kick
scenarios.trigger: If Lookaway leads uncontested and the pace becomes moderate through halfway
scenarios.body: The race develops into a sprint finish where hold-up horses with superior turn of foot can exploit their position. Fresh legs and tactical speed become decisive over raw stamina.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Honest Gallop Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners press Lookaway early and maintain genuine pace throughout
scenarios.body: The searching test plays to the strengths of staying types who can grind out the finish. Stamina becomes more important than tactical speed over the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Early Collapse Setup
scenarios.trigger: If Lookaway goes too fast early under pressure from the prominent pack
scenarios.body: The pace collapses dramatically allowing mid-division runners to inherit a tactical advantage. Horses with patient jockeys can time their runs to perfection from off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Running Success
scenarios.trigger: If Lookaway gets an uncontested lead and stays on strongly in the soft ground
scenarios.body: The leader maintains his advantage to the line as the chasing pack fails to organize an effective challenge. Early position proves decisive in the testing conditions.

races.paceDynamic: Hiddenvalley Lake will take this race forward from the flag with no obvious challengers for the early lead, creating a measured gallop over this stamina-sapping trip. The prominent racers Honesty Policy, Jingko Blue, Strong Leader and Hewick will track the leader in the second rank, while the hold-up horses Home By The Lee, Impose Toi and Take No Chances will rely on being delivered late. With one uncontested leader setting his own fractions, the pace will be sustainable rather than searching, creating perfect conditions for the hold-up brigade to unleash their finishing kicks. This tactical setup strongly favours the patient hold-up horses who can benefit from the even gallop and deliver their best work in the final half-mile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Hiddenvalley Lake sets uncontested fractions and the pace stays steady throughout
scenarios.body: The patient finishers get the perfect setup to unleash their kicks from off the pace. Home By The Lee, Impose Toi and Take No Chances can all deliver their best work when not fighting for position early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Victory
scenarios.trigger: If the Henderson duo Jingko Blue and Doddiethegreat press forward to challenge the pace
scenarios.body: This creates a more searching gallop that suits the prominent racers who can stay close enough to strike. The added pace brings stamina into play over this extended trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Hiddenvalley Lake goes too slow and multiple horses come with late runs
scenarios.body: The finish becomes a sprint where class and recent form matter most. Several horses converge in a bunch finish where positioning and luck become crucial.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Hiddenvalley Lake gets loose on the lead and maintains his kick
scenarios.body: The leader gets first run on the field and holds on grimly despite the late challengers. His stamina reserves prove decisive over this marathon trip.

watchPoints.text: Hiddenvalley Lake could steal a march if given too much rope on the lead and no one challenges early enough

Home By The Lee's position turning for home will be crucial as he needs clear room to deliver his finishing kick
Monitor how aggressively the prominent horses track Hiddenvalley Lake through the early stages
Take No Chances could outrun his odds if the weight allowance proves significant in a tactical affair

races.name: Randox Grand National Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: I Am Maximus
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist perfectly suited to this test, 68 days since last run could be ideal preparation
runners_data.comment: 1st and 2nd in last two Grand Nationals; penultimate race suggests all his ability remains
runners_data.spotlight: His only three long-distance events resulted in an Irish National win in 2023, a storming success in this race in 2024 (soft) and a valiant second, from further off the pace, to Nick Rockett on return to Aintree in 2025 (good to soft); what a record that is, and 50-1 second in a 3m Grade 1 at Leopardstown on penultimate start gives every encouragement that all his ability remains; the return of cheekpieces (tried once in 2022) is interesting but, off 1lb higher than last year, he should be set for another prominent finish.

runners_data.name: Nick Rockett
runners_data.note: Non-runner removes last year's winner from calculations
runners_data.comment: Won this in 2025 in basically smooth style; up 4lb; this year's preparation is a big worry
runners_data.spotlight: Final leg of last season's hat-trick was delivered in basically smooth style here in the National, asserting in the final 1f from I Am Maximus and Grangeclare West (good to soft); 4lb higher today but it's far more concerning that his season has hardly got going, with reappearance delayed until last month when he was seriously ring-rusty behind Gerri Colombe; last year's and this year's build-ups could hardly be more contrasting and he's been deserted by Patrick Mullins.

runners_data.name: Gerri Colombe
runners_data.note: Prominent style risky in this company, long absence from peak form concerning
runners_data.comment: 2nd in 2024 Cheltenham Gold Cup and, some positive signs lately, could be on his way back
runners_data.spotlight: Five Grade 1 wins and runner-up in the 2024 Cheltenham Gold Cup; reappearance at Christmas came after 421 days off and this season's form is well short of his best, but second to Grangeclare West at Fairyhouse was a big step back in the right direction and he comfortably obliged at odds-on for latest outing; cheekpieces last three starts; well handicapped on his old form and could be on his way back.

runners_data.name: Monty's Star
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who keeps trying at top level, 68-day break could freshen him up
runners_data.comment: Trying in vain at Grade 1 level; going up markedly in trip in a handicap is mouthwatering
runners_data.spotlight: Just 1-11 as a chaser, largely because he keeps trying in vain at Grade 1 level; fourth in last year's Cheltenham Gold Cup was one of his peak efforts, as was this season's never-nearer fifth in a Leopardstown Grade 1 at Christmas; he didn't fare so well in the Irish Gold Cup last time but was the only one matching strides with the top-class winner on the home turn; going up markedly in trip today, in a handicap, makes him a mouthwatering proposition.

runners_data.name: Champ Kiely
runners_data.note: Natural front runner who has never raced beyond 3m1f, stamina major question mark
runners_data.comment: Whether he'll stay 4m2f is a big question but he could outrun his odds for a long way
runners_data.spotlight: The furthest he's been is 3m1f in Grade 1 novice at Punchestown Festival (good to yielding) last April which he won in good style, showing improved form; went close over 2m in November and although he slipped up next time and met with heavy defeats twice since, he went well enough to the home turn in Irish Gold Cup on latest; whether he'll stay 4m2f is a big question but he could outrun his odds for a long way.

runners_data.name: Firefox
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with tongue-tie fitted, needs to settle early to be effective
runners_data.comment: Ran on late when fourth in Irish Gold Cup (3m); didn't see out 3m2f so well at Cheltenham
runners_data.spotlight: Tongue tied on last two starts; first time he went beyond 2m5f was also in the Irish Gold Cup at Leopardstown (3m, soft) in February, when 33-1 and spending most of the race out the back but running on into fourth of 12, beaten 14l; some encouragement might be derived from that but he didn't see it out so well when confronted by 3m2f in the Gold Cup at Cheltenham.

runners_data.name: Spillane's Tower
runners_data.note: Non-runner removes another hold-up contender from the equation
runners_data.comment: Won Grade 2 Cotswold Chase; others have achieved more but he's open to further improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Won two Grade 1s in Ireland in spring 2024 during novice chase campaign (2m4f/3m1f, heavy/yielding) and posted first win since in the Grade 2 Cotswold Chase at Cheltenham (3m1f, soft) this January; he was receiving 6lb from close runner-up L'Homme Presse last time and others in this have achieved more, but he's only eight and could still have improvement to come.

runners_data.name: Oscars Brother
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse trained by father-son team, hat-trick winner with National experience
runners_data.comment: Slow early jumping in 3m1f Grade 1 novice at Cheltenham but he made late inroads into 4th
runners_data.spotlight: A first-season novice won the 2022 Grand National when unraced beyond 3m1f and this Irish challenger (who's one year older) bids to repeat the feat; hat-trick this season included two small-field Grade 2s and when his winning sequence came to an end it was in the Grade 1 novice at Cheltenham Festival, where some slow jumping in the early stages left him with plenty to do but he made late inroads to finish fourth; he still looks capable of better and the longer trip could suit.

runners_data.name: Jordans
runners_data.note: Young hold-up horse who stayed on well over 3m1f at this meeting previously
runners_data.comment: Second in the 3m1f Grade 1 novice chase at this meeting last year; below form since
runners_data.spotlight: Twice second in Grade 1 novice events last season, most notably when upped substantially in trip to 3m1f at this meeting; possibilities judged on that performance (unraced over further) and although he's been nowhere near that form since, his closest finish this term came when a staying-on fifth of 18 over 2m7f as a hurdler; just a 7yo but not totally dismissed.

runners_data.name: Iroko
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who was staying-on fourth last year, tongue-tie could help settling
runners_data.comment: Staying-on fourth in 2025 National off 5lb lower; scoped dirty at Cheltenham last month
runners_data.spotlight: Staying-on fourth in last season's Grand National (good to soft) off 5lb lower as just a 7yo; a second crack at it has been his main target this term but he looked better than ever when winning from Firefox in a hot, three-runner race at Ascot (2m5f; second run after wind surgery) in December and had an excuse (scoped dirty) at the Cheltenham Festival last month; has to be in serious calculations.

runners_data.name: The Real Whacker
runners_data.note: Prominent style but 100 days off track raises fitness questions
runners_data.comment: Well handicapped on peak efforts but those past glories may now be too distant
runners_data.spotlight: 11lb below his peak mark and well handicapped judged on best efforts, the most recent of which were over 3m on good ground late in 2024; muted in this three runs this term, only one of which was over fences but he ended up tailed off in that Wetherby race, which he'd won a year earlier; those past glories may now be too distant.

runners_data.name: Quai De Bourbon
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with cheekpieces fitted, stamina proven over extreme distances
runners_data.comment: Third in the 3m5f Irish National last April but completed only four of his eight chases
runners_data.spotlight: Third in the 3m5f Irish National last April, despite an indifferent round of jumping, and third of 16 with cheekpieces at Leopardstown on latest outing was his best form, despite just the 2m5f; kept jumping out to his right in the latter and although a case can be made for him, it would have to gloss over that he's completed only four of his eight chases.

runners_data.name: Grangeclare West
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who finished excellent third here last year despite final fence mistake
runners_data.comment: 3l third last year, after diving at the final fence (up 3lb today); won his latest outing
runners_data.spotlight: Excellent 3l third to Nick Rockett in last year's renewal, somehow renewing his effort after diving at the final fence cost him plenty of momentum; creditable fifth at Sandown just three weeks later and surging clear from Gerri Colombe at Fairyhouse this February, after another last-fence dive, showed that he's at least as good as ever; 3lb higher than 12 months ago but lots to like.

runners_data.name: Johnnywho
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with tongue-tie and cheekpieces, excellent recent form over these fences
runners_data.comment: 2nd and 1st over 3m2f/3m1f at Cheltenham Festivals and wasn't stopping; up 6lb in future
runners_data.spotlight: Fine over these fences in November; laboured from before three out when a well-beaten fifth to Haiti Couleurs in Irish National last April; that was in the mud, though, and his top efforts have been on good to soft; they include his neck second in the 3m2f Kim Muir at Cheltenham last March and, equipped with first-time cheekpieces after wind surgery, a 3m1f win from Jagwar at this year's Festival; able to race here off the same mark as last time (due to go up 6lb) and he wasn't stopping in either of those big races at Cheltenham; seriously considered.

runners_data.name: High Class Hero
runners_data.note: Front runner whose recent form has been disappointing, needs career revival
runners_data.comment: Staying-on third over an extended 3m4f at Sandown (good; 5lb higher today) last April
runners_data.spotlight: One positive is his staying-on third over an extended 3m4f in the bet365 Gold Cup at Sandown (good; 5lb higher today) last April; another is that he's trained by Willie Mullins, who described him in November as likely to be "an ideal type for the Grand National"; after a solid reappearance, he's been pulled up in good handicaps on his last two outings but both were in the mud and he got loose before the latest, which presumably didn't help.

runners_data.name: Captain Cody
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won 32f race previously, recent form mixed but capable of big effort
runners_data.comment: Tremendous response on the run-in to win 4m Scottish National last April; 12lb higher now
runners_data.spotlight: Leopardstown seventh to Favori De Champdou at Christmas was a glimpse of what he's capable of; the performance which really gets the juices flowing, however, came in the Scottish National at Ayr (4m, good to soft) last April when very confidently ridden and unleashed to find a tremendous response on the run-in, cutting down the leader; it's very hard to rule him out after that, despite the 12lb higher mark.

runners_data.name: Jagwar
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse trying extreme distance for first time, tongue-tie and cheekpieces fitted
runners_data.comment: Constant improver; went close when upped to 3m1f at Cheltenham after some jumping errors
runners_data.spotlight: Improved his rating in every one of his eight chases, winning four and that includes the 2m4f Plate at last year's Cheltenham Festival; first venture much beyond 2m5f had to wait until his return to Cheltenham last month, in which he came from out the back to get within half a length of the winner Johnnywho; that showed he stays 3m1f and suggested he's still capable of better, but his jumping contained unnerving moments; wears cheekpieces first time and a half-brother probably stays 4m.

runners_data.name: Banbridge
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with visor fitted, King George form doesn't guarantee National success
runners_data.comment: So nearly won his second King George at Kempton, which doesn't mean this test will suit
runners_data.spotlight: So nearly won his second King George at Kempton over Christmas but, although he's a class act, excelling over 3m on good ground at that speed track doesn't mean that this test will suit him; his moderate late headway in the extended 2m4f Grade 1 Ryanair at Cheltenham last month isn't that persuasive either.

runners_data.name: Imperial Saint
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who is reserve, excellent record over conventional Aintree fences
runners_data.comment: 3 wins over conventional fences here; 3m1f win this January but this trip is a big unknown
runners_data.spotlight: Reserve; novice campaign last season went well, notably over the conventional fences here where he registered three handicap wins (2m/2m4f) and was second at this meeting (3m1f); resumed progress with a win at Haydock (3m1f) this January but badly hampered at the Cheltenham Festival; this trip is a big step into the unknown but he needs a second look.

runners_data.name: Stellar Story
runners_data.note: Prominent style with tongue-tie and blinkers, comfortably beaten in recent starts
runners_data.comment: Unraced beyond 3m2f but has strongly suggested that he has serious stamina; e-w appeal
runners_data.spotlight: Second to Lecky Watson in the 3m Grade 1 novice at Cheltenham last March; while comfortably dismissed in the closing stages of his three starts this winter, the first two of those were Grade 1 events and giving 8lb to Grangeclare West and Gerri Colombe at Fairyhouse (blinkers replaced cheekpieces) on latest outing makes that result look a whole lot better; above all, perhaps, while unraced beyond 3m2f, he has strongly suggested on plenty of occasions that he has serious stamina reserves; each-way appeal.

runners_data.name: Answer To Kayf
runners_data.note: Prominent runner trying marathon distance again after previous failure
runners_data.comment: Faded in a 3m7f race; clearly his best five ratings were registered on soft or heavy going
runners_data.spotlight: Faded into sixth at Punchestown (3m7f) last May on his only attempt at a marathon trip; worth another go, having rallied so well to win a major 3m handicap at Navan in November, but it's a little hard to ignore that clearly his best five ratings have been registered on soft or heavy going, as have all his four wins.

runners_data.name: Lecky Watson
runners_data.note: Prominent style but never raced beyond 3m2f, stamina unproven at this distance
runners_data.comment: Won 3m Grade 1 at Cheltenham last March from Stellar Story; no impact in Ireland this term
runners_data.spotlight: Unraced beyond 3m2f; came into his own as a novice last term, notably in the 3m Grade 1 at Cheltenham Festival which he won by 4l from Stellar Story; no impact at the top level in Ireland this season and he clambered over the final fence on his way to a heavy defeat behind several of today's rivals in a Grade 3 last time, so current prospects don't look so bright.

runners_data.name: Mr Vango
runners_data.note: Front runner with tongue-tie and cheekpieces, excellent record over extreme distances
runners_data.comment: Nothing to prove for stamina or this track, but he cracked alarmingly on last two outings
runners_data.spotlight: Last season's hat-trick culminated in the 4m2f Midlands National and he rallied to go very close against Twig in the 3m2f Becher over these fences on first outing this term; while there was so much to admire to that point, he's cracked with alarming speed in 3m and 4m1f races on his last two outings.

runners_data.name: Three Card Brag
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with cheekpieces, career-best autumn form but flopped at Christmas
runners_data.comment: Career-best form in the autumn; last year's Grand National and latest start are concerns
runners_data.spotlight: Career-best form in the autumn this season, including a win at Cheltenham (3m1f) and second to Panic Attack in the Coral Gold Cup at Newbury (3m2f); flopped when favourite in the Grade 3 won by Grangeclare West at Fairyhouse in February, admittedly after 12 weeks off but there's the additional worry of last year's Grand National in which he was 16-1 and raced very prominently but faded steadily from three out.

runners_data.name: Panic Attack
runners_data.note: Prominent style perfectly suited to handicaps, in career-best form this season
runners_data.comment: 8lb higher than for her big-race win at Newbury (3m2f) but her dominance is hard to forget
runners_data.spotlight: 10yo who is better than ever this term, including with a big handicap double in November in the Paddy Power Gold Cup at Cheltenham (2m4f, soft) and Coral Gold Cup at Newbury (3m2f, good to soft); dropping back to 2m4f, however, was probably not ideal when creditable third in mares' race at Cheltenham last month; 8lb higher than in the Newbury race but her dominance that day is hard to forget.

runners_data.name: Haiti Couleurs
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has won multiple marathons including Welsh National this season
runners_data.comment: Irish and Welsh National winner; Gold Cup was disappointing but he's bounced back before
runners_data.spotlight: In the last 13 months he's won Cheltenham's NH Chase (3m6f), the Irish National (3m5f), a hurdle race, Welsh National (near 3m7f; 12lb higher today) and a Newbury Grade 2; no way can he be ruled out, particularly as he finished well on top in those four chases, but there have also been two major blips this season; latest was in the Cheltenham Gold Cup, for which he was just 6-1 and made most but went to nothing turning for home (writing on the wall four out); however, he's bounced back before, the likely tempo of this race can suit him better and the trip looks like doing so as well.

runners_data.name: Gorgeous Tom
runners_data.note: Front runner whose form has been solid without being spectacular
runners_data.comment: 11l fourth off this mark to Panic Attack at Newbury (3m2f) and stuck to his task very well
runners_data.spotlight: Fourth behind two of these in 3m Grade 1 novice event at Cheltenham last March; ran creditably all three starts this winter, notably 11l fourth of 24 off this mark to Panic Attack at Newbury (3m2f) in November when he stuck to his task very well having been left at the shambolic start; improvement is needed but that race gave encouragement for longer trips and his dam is half-sister to Cappa Bleu who was placed in this race in 2012 and 2013.

runners_data.name: Top Of The Bill
runners_data.note: Prominent style with cheekpieces, veteran in career-best form this winter
runners_data.comment: An excellent, rallying second at Haydock (extended 3m4f) but this is a much stronger race
runners_data.spotlight: One of several who are now in the veteran stage but also in the form of their lives; 7l winner at Haydock (extended 3m1f) in November and returned there with an excellent, rallying second in the Grand National Trial (extended 3m4f, again good to soft) in February; ridden last three starts by Toby McCain-Mitchell; back up 2lb and an interesting prospect for 4m2f but this is a much stronger race.

runners_data.name: Beauport
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with tongue-tie who faded rapidly after three out last year
runners_data.comment: Stays but he was too zestful in this race last year; now tongue tied first time
runners_data.spotlight: Took well to these fences in last year's renewal but subsided rapidly after three out, which might have been surprising for one who'd won a 4m2f Midlands National (March 2024) but he seemed to race a bit too zestfully in the front rank; 3lb lower today, having run respectably on reappearance but moderately in two hurdle races since (wind surgery before latest); now tongue tied first time; a bit to prove.

runners_data.name: Marble Sands
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse having first run for 106 days, needs race fitness
runners_data.comment: A strong-staying winner at Cheltenham (near 3m4f, soft; 5lb higher today) in November
runners_data.spotlight: Negotiated these fences safely in the 2m5f Topham one year ago, albeit fading into 12th; a strong-staying display to win at Cheltenham (near 3m4f, soft; 5lb higher today) in November hints at untapped potential over long distances.

runners_data.name: Perceval Legallois
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist returning after 100-day break, fell early in this race last year
runners_data.comment: Joint-third fav for this in 2025 but fell at the ninth; nothing to shout about this winter
runners_data.spotlight: Won major 3m handicaps at Leopardstown over fences (by 7l, going away) and hurdles before starting joint-third favourite for last year's National, but he fell on the first circuit; it's too early to forget his best performance (Christmas 2024) but with nothing to shout about in his two races this winter, this time he could be an outsider.

runners_data.name: Twig
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with cheekpieces who went close in Becher Chase over these fences
runners_data.comment: A doughty 3m2f win over these fences in the Becher but remote 10th in last year's National
runners_data.spotlight: Second at the 2024 Cheltenham Festival and started this season with two wins, notably by a short head from Mr Vango in the 3m2f Becher over these fences (wore cheekpieces second time); warmed up for this over hurdles after three months off; the Becher performance was doughty stuff but his only go at a marathon trip was last year's National in which he finished a remote tenth, always behind.

runners_data.name: Spanish Harlem
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with tongue-tie and cheekpieces, Willie Mullins stable in form
runners_data.comment: Stays long distances; his revised mark since bold show in the Thyestes is the chief worry
runners_data.spotlight: Career with Willie Mullins took a long time to catch fire but it's done so this season and he looked set for victory in the Thyestes at Gowran Park (3m1f, heavy) in January when unseating at the final fence; pulled up behind Grangeclare West last time but back catalogue includes a creditable sixth in the Scottish National and fourth in bet365 Cup at Sandown, so he stays long distances; his revised mark since the Thyestes would be the chief worry.

runners_data.name: Pied Piper
runners_data.note: Non-runner removes hold-up horse who has fallen in last two starts
runners_data.comment: Outbattled over 3m1f in October; it's doubtful whether he's got what it takes for this
runners_data.spotlight: Gained all three chase wins in small-field novice events last April-June (one over 2m7f) but fell in three of his nine races since, including the last two; placed over 2m1f as a hurdler at three Cheltenham Festivals and runner-up in a 2m2f Cesarewitch on Flat, but he was outbattled over 3m1f at Cheltenham in October; it's doubtful whether he's got what it takes for this.

runners_data.name: Favori De Champdou
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with blinkers having tremendous season, made most when winning at Christmas
runners_data.comment: 11yo who's having a tremendous season, over Cheltenham cross-country on last two outings
runners_data.spotlight: Experienced 11yo who's having a tremendous season; 66-1 winner of a top 3m handicap at Leopardstown (made most) over Christmas and took his form to another new level on the 3m5f Cheltenham cross-country course on last two outings, winning easily on first occasion and well clear of the third when he chased home Final Orders at last month's Festival; well handicapped and with the trip likely to suit, he's a leading contender.

runners_data.name: Final Orders
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with vast experience over 70 career starts, recent cross-country winner
runners_data.comment: Has taken so well to Cheltenham cross-country; best performances away from soft ground
runners_data.spotlight: 10yo who's had 70 races (only one of today's rivals has managed even half that) and won 11; latest was the 3m5f cross-country at Cheltenham Festival, comfortably holding off Favori De Champdou for career-best form off the same mark as today; having taken so well to that discipline (he also won there in December) and produced his best performances away from soft ground, he has to be considered seriously.

runners_data.name: Amirite
runners_data.note: Reserve with prominent style and tongue-tie, solid record over these fences previously
runners_data.comment: A fluent fourth in the Topham over these fences last April; ran creditably once at 3m4f
runners_data.spotlight: Reserve; a fluent fourth in the 2m5f Topham over these fences was the first of three big runs in good handicaps last April-July; ran creditably in one (Sandown in April 2024) of his three attempts at 3m4f-3m5f and excuses might be made for his latest two outings (first cross-country, then the mud) but other candidates are more persuasive.

races.paceDynamic: Champ Kiely, Mr Vango, High Class Hero and Gorgeous Tom will ensure a genuine gallop from the start over this marathon trip. The strong early pace combined with Aintree's unique fences will stretch the field and test stamina reserves to the maximum. With 15 runners wanting prominent positions but only limited racing room, traffic problems are inevitable approaching the business end. This searching test strongly favours hold-up horses who can avoid the early scrimmaging and finish with one sustained run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the strong early gallop sets up perfectly for closers
scenarios.body: The genuine pace will stretch the field and allow patient riders to pick off tiring leaders in the final mile. Stamina and tactical positioning become decisive factors over this extreme distance.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Success
scenarios.trigger: If one of the handy horses avoids the traffic and finds clear run
scenarios.body: A horse racing in fourth or fifth can strike at the perfect moment when the leaders tire but before the hold-up horses arrive. This requires expert timing and clear sailing from three out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If the early leaders slow the pace tactically mid-race
scenarios.body: A canny front runner could steal a march by steadying the gallop after halfway then kicking again approaching the final circuit. The pursuing pack fails to organize an effective challenge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Carnage Benefits Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers and interference create chaos in the field
scenarios.body: The race becomes a survival test where a lesser-fancied horse with safe jumping finds themselves in contention by default. Navigation skills matter more than raw ability.

watchPoints.text: Multiple fallers likely given large field and unique Aintree obstacles - could eliminate market leaders
Traffic problems inevitable from three out with 15 horses wanting prominent positions and limited racing room
Champ Kiely and High Class Hero both front runners with stamina doubts beyond 3m1f
I Am Maximus seeking back-to-back victories with classic hold-up style perfectly suited to race dynamics
Three non-runners reduce field size but Willie Mullins still has seven representatives in race

races.paceDynamic: Bass Hunter, Look Me, The Perfect Poet, Merry Away, One Knight, Forthfactor and Ronnie Russet will create a fierce early gallop in this Grade 2 contest. Seven confirmed front-runners in a 20-runner field guarantees breakneck fractions over the first mile, with the soft ground adding extra stamina demands. The pace will fragment the field early, creating a stop-start rhythm that punishes those trapped wide or struggling to keep tabs. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can stay out of the early carnage and finish powerfully when others tire.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Profit
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners go too hard early and fade from 2f out...
scenarios.body: The relentless early gallop sets up perfectly for closers who avoided the pace battle. Horses like Merlin Allen, Risky Obsession, and Chicker can pick off tired leaders in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If a horse can track the pace without getting involved in the early battle...
scenarios.body: Smart prominent runners like Smile John Boy or Le Roi Remi can position perfectly behind the speed duel. They get first run on the tiring leaders while the hold-up horses have too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one pace-setter can break clear and find a softer lead after the initial dash...
scenarios.body: Bass Hunter or One Knight could exploit their class advantage by dictating terms once rivals tire. The soft ground plays to their stamina reserves if they can moderate the gallop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners go suicidally fast and all come back dramatically...
scenarios.body: The entire pace contingent ties up badly, leaving a messy finish for any horse with energy left. This creates chaos where long-priced runners can emerge from the pack.

watchPoints.text: Bass Hunter and One Knight must prove they can handle the early pace pressure they'll create themselves.
Merlin Allen needs to overcome 49-day absence but his hold-up style perfectly suits this tactical setup.
Multiple Ben Pauling runners (The Perfect Poet, Merry Away, Smile John Boy) could employ different tactics to exploit the pace.
Several hold-up horses like Risky Obsession and Chicker returning from breaks need to prove fitness first time back.
The 4yo weight allowance for Merlin Allen and Nightflyer becomes crucial if the race becomes a stamina test.
